_comment: Input for tools/generate-slice-prompts.sh. One entry per independently mergeable pre-1.0 slice. Everything else in the generated prompts is derived from the repository, not from this file.

slices.title: Decide where logging ownership actually lives
slices.description: ErrorHandlerLib calls error_log() directly in three places while README claims logging is host-controlled. Decide between correcting the README, adding one narrow integration logging method, or moving logging fully behind ErrorHandlerIntegrationInterface, and implement exactly one of them without weakening sanitizeErrorDetails().

slices.title: Prove the supported PHP range in CI
slices.description: composer.json requires php ^8.3 but .github/workflows/ci.yml only runs 8.3 and 8.4. Extend the matrix so the declared range is actually proven, and treat any PHP 8.5 error-handling difference as compatibility evidence rather than papering over it.

slices.title: Host ergonomics around the skip decider
slices.description: Evaluate whether consumers already need more than one skip rule, whether ErrorHandlerSkipDeciderInterface is named accurately now that PHP suppression is a separate policy, and whether resetDefaults() gives tests deterministic isolation. Add a composable skip decider only if current consumer evidence mechanically requires it.

slices.title: Audit developer-facing diagnostic output
slices.description: Inspect stack-trace generation and error-detail formatting for concrete defects only: duplicate frames, the same details reaching both error_log() and the renderer, accidental argument or secret exposure, oversized argument rendering, and error-handler recursion. Never weaken sanitizeErrorDetails() or start exposing arbitrary object or request contents to improve debugging.

slices.title: Pin handleError() return semantics against PHP handler chaining
slices.description: handleError() reads ini_get('display_errors') directly instead of asking the integration, and its true/false return decides whether PHP's internal handler also runs. Establish and test the exact contract for every path: critical, suppressed-and-ignored, application-skipped, warning, and notice.
